assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Start with a numerical semigroup S. By standard semigroup facts, the conductor c exists, the set L = S ∩ [0,c-1] is finite, and the minimal generating set exists and has finite cardinality e. Next count the integers in [0,c-1]: those in S contribute |L| and those outside S contribute g, so c = |L| + g. Rearranging shows that the desired inequality e|L| >= c is equivalent to (e-1)|L| >= g. At this point the argument reaches the classical Wilf conjecture in genus form. Since no general proof of that final inequality is known, the decomposition cannot honestly be completed into a proof of the universal root theorem using only true established lemmas.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Provides the basic existence of the conductor appearing in the root theorem.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup, meaning that S is a subset of the nonnegative integers, 0 belongs to S, S is closed under addition, and the complement Z_{>=0} \ S is finite. Then there exists a unique integer c >= 0 such that c belongs to S, every integer n >= c belongs to S, and c-1 does not belong to S unless c = 0. Equivalently, the set { n in Z_{>=0} : for all m >= n, m belongs to S } is nonempty and has a least element, called the conductor of S.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Supplies finiteness and meaning of the quantity |L| in the root theorem.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup, let c be its conductor, and define L := { s in S : s < c }. Then L is a finite set and 0 belongs to L unless c = 0. Moreover, |L| is a well-defined nonnegative integer.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Provides the well-definedness of e in the root theorem.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup. An element x in S \ {0} is called a minimal generator if x cannot be written as a sum a + b with a and b in S \ {0}. Then the set MinGen(S) of minimal generators is finite, it generates S as an additive submonoid of Z_{>=0}, and every generating set of S contains MinGen(S). In particular, the number e := |MinGen(S)| is a well-defined positive integer, called the embedding dimension of S.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Records a standard structural tool often used in proofs of special cases of Wilf-type inequalities.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with multiplicity m, where m is the least positive element of S. For each residue class r modulo m, define Ap(S,m,r) to be the least element of S congruent to r modulo m, and define the Apéry set Ap(S,m) := { w in S : w - m is not in S }. Then Ap(S,m) has exactly m elements, one in each residue class modulo m, and max(Ap(S,m)) = c + m - 1 where c is the conductor of S.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Gives the elementary counting identity c = |L| + g.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with conductor c and let L := { s in S : s < c }. Then the genus g := | { n in Z_{>=0} : n < c and n not in S } | satisfies |L| + g = c. Equivalently, among the integers 0,1,...,c-1, exactly |L| of them lie in S and exactly g of them lie outside S.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Reformulates the target inequality into the standard genus form.
lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup with embedding dimension e, conductor c, and L := { s in S : s < c }. The inequality e * |L| >= c is exactly equivalent to the inequality (e - 1) * |L| >= g, where g := | { n in Z_{>=0} : n < c and n not in S } | is the number of gaps below the conductor.

shared_context.content: The root theorem is the classical Wilf conjecture: for a numerical semigroup S with embedding dimension e, conductor c, and L = S ∩ [0,c-1], one has e * |L| >= c. This statement is open in full generality as of the present date, although many special cases are known.

payload.theorem_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup. Let e be the number of minimal generators of S, let c be the smallest integer such that every integer greater than or equal to c belongs to S, and let L be the set of elements of S that are strictly less than c. Then e multiplied by the number of elements of L is at least c.
